prompt: Style: a hand-made fantasy concept painting, the kind a game's art team makes while designing its world: a loose graphite and ink drawing with gestural, broken, searching lines left visible under transparent washes of muted watercolor and a few strokes of opaque gouache, on warm toned paper whose grain shows through. The porch, the brazier and the sleeping dog are drawn with care; the village, the mill and the mountains behind are suggested with fewer, looser marks and soft washes, and some edges are left unfinished. A limited palette: slate blue, blue-gray and bone white, the warm amber of the fire as the one accent. The scene: one locked-off wide shot at standing eye height from the covered timber porch of a log house in a Riverwood-style Nordic river village, looking out across a calm river to a log sawmill with its big wooden waterwheel, a pine forest and snowcapped mountains under the northern lights. The porch has no railing: two thick timber posts and the roof beam frame the view. Foreground: rough porch planks with carved beam ends above; the hound asleep on its wolf fur at the lower left, an arm's length from the brazier, so the fire and the dog stay apart; the brazier's fire low and calm. Midground: below the porch a low, level bank of gravel and flat stones runs along the water's edge from left to right, with a mossy boulder at each end; then the dark, calm river, and on its far bank the log sawmill at the right of center with its undershot waterwheel at its side: the wheel's hub, spokes and paddles stand out clearly against the mill's dark wall, its lowest paddles dip into the river and no water pours onto it from above; two log houses of the village further along the far bank with a few warmly lit small windows. Background: a dark pine forest rising to snowcapped mountains; above them the northern lights: soft green curtains with faint violet upper edges across the upper part of the sky, open clear night sky with a few stars around them, no moon; the river faintly mirrors the green of the lights. Real darkness: deep blue night over most of the frame; the brazier's small fire and the lantern light the porch warmly and fall off within a few meters; the northern lights cast a faint cold green on the snow, the mill's roof and the river. The porch posts frame the view at both sides; the waterwheel and the northern lights are the focal point, a little right of center; the hound and the brazier sit low in the frame, apart from each other; quiet open sky and calm water around the wheel and the lights. Locked-off camera at eye level, wide 16:9 composition with a clear foreground, midground and background. Leave open, uncluttered areas around the light sources, the windows and the animal so they can be animated. No people anywhere: no pedestrians or silhouettes outside, no portraits, posters or statues of people. No other animals besides the one pet: no birds, insects, snails or frogs anywhere (small creatures are animated in afterwards). No lightning bolts. Things that move are animated afterwards, so do not paint them frozen: no visible steam or smoke plumes, no water drops hanging from edges and no streams of dripping water; surfaces may look wet. No text, no letters, no logos, no watermark, no user interface. It must look like deliberate work by an artist, never generic AI fantasy art: no glossy or plastic surfaces, no sparkles or glitter, no bokeh, no lens flare, no bloom halos, no glowing particles, sparks or dust motes, no god rays, no wet reflections full of glints, no teal-and-orange grading, no HDR detail on every surface, no smooth airbrushed gradients, no epic fantasy-poster drama. Leave large areas simple and dark; put the detail only where the eye should go.
